To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complexity of the BPW model is not a fundamental obstacle to using it in practice, that the BPW model can be formalized and used in Isabelle/HO L, and that our abstractions are a useful tool for reasoning about cryptographic protocols in the symbolic model.

we have (1) developed a formal theory that supports cryptographically-sound protocol modeling and (2) shown that this formal theory can be used to prove security properties of protocols that are comparable in complexity to those based on standard models.

we present a formal theory of cryptographically-sounds symbolic protocol models, which includes an abstraction hierarchy that brings the complexity of these models much closer to that of standard DolevYao style models, and that we have formalized this development in Isabelle/HO L.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have formalized and used a cryptographically-sound protocol-model abstraction that is close enough to Dolev-Yoa models that it can be practically used for protocol proofs.

we have shown how to use the original BPW formalization to prove a number of security theorems, including some of the more complex and important ones, and that we can do this in a way that is much more efficient than using the full BPW model directly.
the BPW model is not a practical basis for formal verification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the original BPW protocol model is too complex to use for formal verification of cryptographic protocols.

we have developed a cryptographically sound symbolic model for protocol proofs and we have developed a set of abstractions of this model that bring it close to the standard models used in the protocol verification community.

we provide a formal theory for proving security in the presence of active attacks, which is based on a cryptographically sound symbolic protocol model and is as convenient to use as standard Dolev Yao models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve cryptographically sound proofs without having to resort to the full power of the original BPWs model.
the complexity of cryptographically-sounds models can be significantly reduced, while still preserving the cryptographic soundness.
cryptographically-sound models can be made much more usable by carefully choosing abstractions that are appropriate for the task at hand.
